A surface trough of low pressure (the remnants of Tropical Storm  Dolly) is producing a disorganized area of showers and thunderstorms  that extends from near Hispaniola eastward to the northern Leeward  Islands. Redevelopment, if any, would be slow to occur during the  next few days as the system encounters generally unfavorable  upper-level winds while moving quickly west-northwestward at 20 to  25 mph. Regardless, the system could bring locally heavy rains and  gusty winds to portions of the Leeward Islands, the Virgin Islands,  Puerto Rico, Hispaniola, and the Bahamas during the next couple of  days. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

An area of low pressure located a little more than 100 miles south  of the coast of southern Louisiana continues to produce a small but  concentrated area of showers and thunderstorms with some signs of  organization. Additional development is expected as the low moves  slowly west-northwestward, and a short-lived tropical depression or  tropical storm is likely to form before the system reaches the Upper  Texas or southwestern Louisiana coasts on Tuesday.  1. Interests along the southwestern Louisiana and Upper Texas coasts  should monitor the progress of this system, as tropical storm  watches or warnings could be required for portions of the area later  today. Regardless of development, this system is expected to bring  locally heavy rainfall to portions of the Upper Texas and  southwestern Louisiana coasts during the next couple of days. An Air  Force Reserve reconnaissance aircraft is scheduled to investigate  the system this morning. Additional information on this system,  including gale warnings, can be found in High Seas Forecasts issued  by the National Weather Service. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Showers and thunderstorms are showing signs of organization in  association with a broad area of low pressure located several  hundred miles south-southwest of the coast of southwestern Mexico.   Environmental conditions are conducive for development, and a  tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form later  today or tonight, while the system moves northwestward around 10  mph. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the  Hawaiian Islands in a couple of days. Some gradual development is  possible thereafter while it moves slowly and erratically. 
 Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. 
 Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.
